title: State-of-the-art retinal vessel segmentation with minimalistic models (W-Net)
mechanism: A tiny carefully trained U-Net nearly matches complex SOTA; a cascade (second net sees image + first prediction) reaches SOTA; most complete cross-dataset study (10 sets).
adaptation: W-Net cascade as the cheapest refinement stage: second small U-Net on [EL, 24-class softmax of the house model], trained on the frozen first stage or jointly. Compare against a 2-model ensemble to separate cascade from ensembling.
min_experiment: Arm: house + second-stage refiner, 5 seeds; baseline: 2-model house ensemble (compute-matched). Metric crack relF1@2, inactive IoU, mIoU_rob. Kill: relF1@2 gain < 0.01 vs the matched ensemble.
evidence: Minimal U-Net close to best methods; W-Net SOTA on several vessel sets with orders of magnitude fewer weights; cross-dataset performance drops a lot; self-labelling gave moderate cross-domain gain.
prior_overlap: none; refinement networks listed as never tried

alt_notes.adaptation: Benchmark design: strong simple baselines, a rigorous protocol and a mandatory unseen-domain test (E1). For scores: a W-Net style second U-Net that takes the image and the first-stage probabilities.
alt_notes.min_experiment: W-Net cascade on house vs house, 5 seeds. Metrics: crack relF1@2 and E1 recall. Kill if gains < 0.012.
